subject: RE: Appriss SSO & Incident
body:
EXTERNAL SENDER


Thank you again Shelley for setting up the call today to discuss SSO/SSO+ along with some of the open support tickets. J.R. – it was nice speaking with you and meeting you as well. We appreciate the support and changes that are going to be made.

 

Just to confirm, the daily file feed should handle all the permissions - I just want to double check with Mike first that we are okay to remove the existing SSO+ entries. You can hold off on doing that for now, but I should be able to confirm if we want to do that in the next few days.

 

Any questions, comments, or concerns, please let me know.

 

Thanks again,

 

Colton Neal (He/Him/His)

Subject: RE: Appriss SSO & Incident 

 

Hi Colton,

Thank you for your patience, I have a good update for you. We're now ingesting the SSO files into Incident, which resolves the permissions issue you raised. With this in place, the following are assigned to users automatically from the feed:
- Location(s)
- Permission groups and teams
- Incident roles

One thing to flag: a small number of users may have an existing SSO+ entry that takes precedence over what comes through in the file feed. We can’t tell which of those entries were set intentionally versus created out of necessity, so if you spot a user whose assignments don't look right, send their name our way and we'll take a look.  We can chat through this as well on our call today, so that you know what to look for as a sign that an SSO+ entry is taking precedence over file load.  More importantly, if you can confirm that the file feed should be handling all permissions, we can systematically do a one time removal of the existing SSO+ entries.

As part of bringing these files in, we identified a few areas to tighten up on our side, so we'll be monitoring closely over the next several days to confirm everything is running smoothly and to put better early-warning checks in place. I'll keep you posted, and please let me know if you run into anything in the meantime.

Cheers,

Shelley Cameron
